L4@P0-1: ANIMAL WELFARE POLICYLatest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L5@P1: Version Number 2.0 Page 2 of 5
L6@P1: Public Copy
L7@P1: BACKGROUND
L8@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to using responsibly sourced raw materials including the
L9@P1: use of products derived from animals. This policy forms part of our commitment to uphold
L10@P1: the M&S animal welfare principles for all animal derived products we source.
L11@P1: SCOPE
L12@P1: This policy covers products sold in all Clothing, Home and Beauty areas that contain any
L13@P1: animal derived raw materials. The scope includes all main fabrics/textiles, trims,
L14@P1: componentry packaging, chemicals, pigments and dyestuffs.
L15@P1: This policy is intended to complement the additional specific sourcing policies for
L16@P1: Cashmere, Wool, Leather and Feather and Down.
L17@P1: RATONALE AND OBJECTIVES
L18@P1: • To ensure Marks & Spencer meets its long-standing commitment to improve animal
L19@P1: welfare in its supply chains and ensure all animal derived materials are sourced from
L20@P1: farms with good animal welfare practices. Marks & Spencer are committed to
L21@P1: improving animal welfare across our global supply chains and we are working to
L22@P1: source all animal-derived materials from farms with good animal welfare practices
L23@P1: • To lay out a set of uniform principles and guidelines around the sourcing of animal
L24@P1: derived raw materials
L25@P1: • To also ensure that appropriate due diligence is undertaken with regards to the
L26@P1: sourcing of products in relation to animal welfare
L27@P1: M&S MANDATORY PRINCIPLES FOR SOURCING
L28@P1: Marks and Spencer are committed to protecting any endangered or vulnerable species and
L29@P1: to the prevention of cruelty. Through our supply chains we seek to promote, encourage and
L30@P1: foster higher animal welfare standards using codes, recommendations and audited supply
L31@P1: chains. We will continuously review our supply chains and where there are practices that
L32@P1: are of concern, we will take a considered course of action.
L33@P1: No animal will be slaughtered specifically for the manufacture or sourcing of M&S products.
L34@P1: PROHIBITED SOURCES
L35@P1: The following materials do not comply with our business principles for animal welfare and
L36@P1: therefore must not be used in any of our non-food products:
L37@P1: • Any material from any endangered species, defined as those which appear on the
L38@P1-2: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) (see www.cites.org/ Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L39@P2: Version Number 2.0 Page 3 of 5
L40@P2: Public Copy
L41@P2: for list of species) or the IUCN red list as Critically Endangered,
L42@P2: Endangered or Vulnerable (www.redlist.org/).
L43@P2: • No animal must be slaughtered specifically to produce any non- food M&S products.
L44@P2: • Fur: this includes farmed fur (e.g. fox, sable, mink, chinchilla, rabbit)
L45@P2: • Angora Rabbit fibre
L46@P2: • Alpaca fibre
L47@P2: • Astrakhan (Karakul) or any other leather/skin products which are the product of
L48@P2: unnatural abortions
L49@P2: • Any material obtained from live skinning (e.g. reptiles) or live boiling
L50@P2: • Any cow hides sourced from India
L51@P2: • Any animal derived bone or horn
L52@P2: • Any down or feathers from exotic birds, including but not limited to ostrich
L53@P2: • Any coral
L54@P2: RESTRICTED SOURCES
L55@P2: The following materials are currently accepted provided minimum requirements are met:
L56@P2: • Leather must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible Leather Sourcing Policy
L57@P2: • Animal Fibres (e.g. wool, cashmere) must be sourced in compliance with our Responsible
L58@P2: Wool Sourcing Policy and our Cashmere Code of Practice for animal welfare respectively.
L59@P2: All wool must be sourced from sheep that have not been mulesed
L60@P2: • Mohair must only be sourced through routes fully certified to the Textile Exchange
L61@P2: Responsible Mohair Standard (RMS)
L62@P2: • Feather and Down must not be obtained from the live plucking of birds or from birds used
L63@P2: in the production of Foie Gras. All Feather and Down must be sourced in compliance to
L64@P2: our Responsible Feather and Down Sourcing Policy
L65@P2: • All other animal derived materials must be sourced in accordance with this policy and
L66@P2: relevant details must be provided on an Animal derived material declaration form
L67@P2: • Any shell from vulnerable or endangered species must not be used (as defined by
L68@P2: CITES/IUCN red list)
L69@P2-3: • Only pearls form cultivated sources are allowed Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L70@P3: Version Number 2.0 Page 4 of 5
L71@P3: Public Copy
L72@P3: THE FIVE FREEDOMS OF ANIMAL WELFARE
L73@P3: In developing minimum standards for sourcing any animal product Marks & Spencer
L74@P3: consider the internationally recognised “Five Freedoms” as a framework and for guidance. It
L75@P3: is important that the sourcing of any animal derived materials for M&S are underpinned by
L76@P3: these principles:
L77@P3: 1. Freedom from Hunger and Thirst – by ready access to fresh water and a diet to
L78@P3: maintain full health and vigour
L79@P3: 2. Freedom from Discomfort – by providing an appropriate environment including
L80@P3: shelter and a comfortable resting area
L81@P3: 3. Freedom from Pain, Injury and Disease – by prevention or rapid diagnosis and
L82@P3: treatment
L83@P3: 4. Freedom to Express Normal Behaviour – by providing sufficient space, proper
L84@P3: facilities and company of the animal’s own kind
L85@P3: 5. Freedom from Fear and Distress – by ensuring conditions and treatment which
L86@P3: avoid mental suffering
L87@P3: ANIMAL TESTING
L88@P3: Marks and Spencer will not conduct or commission any tests on animals. All M&S own brand
L89@P3: cosmetic and household products and ingredients must be approved by the BUAV under
L90@P3: the Humane Cosmetics Standard, The Leaping Bunny Standard. This standard has been in
L91@P3: place since January 2006
L92@P3: PET ACCESSORIES
L93@P3: Any pet accessories are subject to all mandatory principles for sourcing. In addition, the
L94@P3: product itself must not compromise the welfare of the animal for which it is intended to be
L95@P3: used, using the Five Freedoms as a reference.
L96@P3: PRODUCT PROMOTION
L97@P3: Marks and Spencer will review all animal imagery used in the promotion of its products to
L98@P3: ensure that it does not endorse animal exploitation, cruelty or irresponsible use or
L99@P3: ownership.
L100@P3: DEFINITIONS
L101@P3: Animals: The Vegan Society understands the word animal to refer to the entire animal
L102@P3-4: kingdom, that is all vertebrates and multi-cellular invertebrates. The word may be used either Latest Version Date June 2020 Doc Ref Animal Welfare Policy
L103@P4: Version Number 2.0 Page 5 of 5
L104@P4: Public Copy
L105@P4: as a noun or an adjective and to refer to a species, or an individual animal,
L106@P4: depending on context.
L107@P4: Animal derived materials: Materials including ingredients that have an animal (see above
L108@P4: definition), origin, regardless of whether they have been harvested form live or dead
L109@P4: animals.
